answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with rewards released only after the job is verified and disputes expire. A zephyr of freshly minted accounts then gains no cheap influence: each one ties up real capital, and invalid work risks forfeiting the stake. The lotus registry can track those locks, while pigment marks verified history without letting reputation alone create identities. This raises the cost of an attack in proportion to the number and duration of accounts.
